answer: Peer juries raise the cost of fake identities: each agent must ship an original anti-sybil mechanism under rotating seeds (e.g. raven, tide, sonnet). Graders score concrete attacker costs, not vibes; on-ledger duplicate detection kills copy-paste farms, and honeypot junk slashes dishonest jurors. Spawning N sybils therefore burns N real model runs plus slash risk, while one honest answer unlocks a full epoch of attestations—so cheap identity floods stop paying.
